summary: Round-2 re-review of the two round-1 fixes in FunnelMessagePreview.spec.ts. Both fixes are correct, behavior-driven, and free of false-positive risk. The new empty-renderedBlocks desync test exercises the real defensive branch (keyboardText computed returns null on missing TEXT block, mock absent on null keyboardRows, panel still mounts) and would catch a crash or an unconditional renderedBlocks[0] access. The debounce test now pairs call-count gating with toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(objectContaining(...)), proving the mutated keyboardText/keyboardRows actually propagated into the payload rather than only that a call fired. Spec re-run green: 29 tests, up from 28. No blocking or major findings.

findings.issue: The keyboardRows propagation assertion uses objectContaining({ keyboardRows: [{ buttons: [{ text: 'B' }] }] }) which only confirms the mutated rows reached the payload; it does not also re-assert keyboardText remains 'Новий текст'. Coverage is correct but the test does not pin that the unchanged sibling field is preserved across the second debounce, so a future regression that drops keyboardText during a rows-only edit would go unnoticed by this test (the dedicated text assertion is on the earlier setProps, with a different rendered value). Non-blocking — the payload-shape test at line 499 already locks the full SET_KEYBOARD payload shape.
findings.recommendation: Optional: widen the last assertion to objectContaining({ keyboardText: 'Новий текст', keyboardRows: [{ buttons: [{ text: 'B' }] }] }) so the rows-only edit also proves the carried-over text field is preserved in the same payload.
